title: Gear for Gold
description: Gear for Gold strengthens athlete-centric academies across India with sports science, infrastructure, technology, and performance systems.
lede: Gear for Gold strengthens athlete-centric academies across India by supporting them with sports science, infrastructure, technology, and performance systems to drive long-term excellence.

image.alt: Training session underway on the courts of a partner badminton academy

paragraphs: Gear for Gold, an initiative of the Infosys Foundation, is designed to build stronger, athlete-centric academies across India. By using GoSports' Academy Development Model, the programme empowers academies, enables coaches, and drives athlete development for long-term sporting excellence.

partnership.heading: A flagship collaboration
paragraphs: Gear for Gold is a flagship partnership between Infosys Foundation and GoSports Foundation, designed to strengthen athlete-centric academies across India. Building on the Girls for Gold initiative, the programme now supports male, female, and para-athletes across Olympic disciplines.

quote.quote: "Infosys Foundation and GoSports Foundation share a joint passion for strengthening the sports ecosystem in India. We are delighted with the progress we have made together in nurturing exceptional youngsters across sporting disciplines."
quote.name: Sumit Virmani
quote.role: Global Chief Marketing Officer, Infosys; Trustee, Infosys Foundation

numbers.footnote: 130+ high-performance camps delivered across the year.

academies.heading: Eight academies at the heart of the programme
academies.intro: Gear for Gold works through eight athlete-centric academies, most of them founded by Olympians and national coaches who now develop the next generation.

items.name: Lakshya Shooting Club
items.text: Founded by Olympian and Dronacharya awardee Suma Shirur: a high-performance centre for 10m and 50m shooting.

items.name: Mary Kom Regional Boxing Foundation
items.text: Set up by Olympic medallist Mary Kom, with residential training for boxers from across the region.

items.name: Raman Table Tennis High Performance Centre
items.text: Founded by Olympian and Dronacharya awardee S. Raman with former national player Bhuvaneswari B.

items.name: Yadav Pro Badminton Academy
items.text: Founded by former international shuttler Jagadish Yadav and recognised under Khelo India.

items.name: Sathish Sivalingam Sports Foundation
items.text: Founded by Olympian and Arjuna awardee Sathish Sivalingam after his 2018 Commonwealth Games gold.

items.name: Usha School of Athletics
items.text: Founded by Olympian P.T. Usha to train young women athletes in sprints, jumps and middle distance.

items.name: Malik Badminton Academy
items.text: Founded by Harender Malik, with a structured grassroots-to-international pathway open to underprivileged players.

items.name: Karnam Malleswari Foundation
items.text: Founded by Olympic bronze medallist Karnam Malleswari, with coaching, nutrition and residential support.

pillars.heading: Pillars of the Academy Development Model

items.title: Athlete development pathway
items.text: A structured system to identify, train, progress, and transition athletes across levels.

items.title: Coaching & support ecosystem
items.text: A tech-driven, integrated support ecosystem around athletes training at the academy.

items.title: Infrastructure & sports science
items.text: International-standard facilities and performance centres built for athlete and coach development.

items.title: Governance & programme management
items.text: Clear governance frameworks that drive decision-making, accountability, and effective delivery.

items.quote: "This programme takes a holistic approach — supporting both athletes and coaches. Even at an early stage, it is already showing strong results."
items.name: Peter Davis

items.quote: "The high-performance training camp in Germany helped me refine both technical and mental aspects of my performance. Every session pushed me to grow."
items.name: Khyati Chaudhury

items.quote: "Coaches now have the opportunity to travel with athletes to tournaments and understand current standards — this helps us identify gaps and work on improvement."
items.name: Harender Malik
items.role: Founder & Head Coach, Malik Badminton Academy
